recipes.name: Chef John's Asparagus Souffle
ingredients_raw: 1 bunch asparagus, trimmed and cut into 1/2-inch pieces
1 pinch cayenne pepper, or to taste
0.5 cup grated sharp white Cheddar cheese

steps.text: Cook asparagus in a saucepan of boiling water until bright green but still crisp, about 2 minutes. Transfer asparagus to ice water to stop the cooking process. Drain and set aside.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium-low heat. Whisk in flour and stir until mixture becomes paste-like and light golden brown, about 2 minutes.
Whisk milk into butter-flour mixture; bring to a simmer and cook until thick, 2 to 3 minutes. Season with salt and cayenne pepper.
Place milk mixture, garlic, and asparagus in a blender and puree until smooth.
Pour asparagus mixture into a large bowl; stir in egg yolks and Cheddar cheese.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C)
Beat egg whites in a large glass or metal mixing bowl until soft peaks form. Lift your beater or whisk straight up: the egg whites will form soft mounds rather than a sharp peak
Stir half of egg whites into asparagus cheese mixture until just combined. Gently fold remaining egg whites into mixture.
Fill prepared ramekins about 3/4 full and place on a baking sheet; bake in the preheated oven until edges are golden brown, about 20 to 25 minutes

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John's Asparagus Souffle
raw_recipe.description: Fresh asparagus and sharp white Cheddar cheese give this savory souffle its bright color and bold flavors.

review.reviewBody: This was really easy!! Yay!! I was nervous because this was my first souffle. I doubled the recipe with the exception of the eggs. (I only used one extra because I ran out. It still worked.) The only thing I would add is more asparagus than called for. I will most definitely cook this again.
This was fantastic - I placed phyllo dough squares in a muffin pan and then poured souffle in the cups - made for an awesome looking veg dish that was delicious.

Based on some review comments about a lack of flavor, I used a combination of White Cheddar Cheese and Asiago cheese. I also added 1/4 tsp of dried basil and some freshly ground black pepper. An immersion blender worked well to puree the asparagus and milk/egg mixture.

Really good! I added 2 extra egg whites and some chopped ham. Also used 1 cup Gruyere instead of 1/2 cup Cheddar. Finally, used a large souffle dish instead of individual ramekins and baked for 30 minutes.

4 stars because I changed it up a bit. I used spinach and some chopped cauliflower (husband doesn't like asparagus), didn't use the blender, and made in an 8" square baking dish. That meant that it didn't "rise" like a normal souffle, but still the proportions and timing worked well. I've made similar ones just with spinach; this one got raves from my husband. Thanks Chef John, always good recipes from you!

Reading some of the reviews and one of the major beefs is that the soufflés didn't stay puffed up or inflated for very long. DUH! It's a soufflé, they all deflate within seconds of pulling them out of the oven be it sweet or savory. If people would watch Chef John's videos attached with the recipe, he gives you a step-by-step, play-by-play tutorial of each of his recipes. You can use any kind of cheese that suits you and season to your liking. We don't like cayenne pepper and I would switch that with nutmeg because that is what I always use in bechsmel and green veggies to enhance the flavor. Just a little goes a long way and if you don't like nutmeg, you won't even know that it's there if you use just a smidgen (1/32 tsp which is the exact measurement of a "smidgen"). I can't wait to try this! We love asparagus and who doesn't love a light and fluffy soufflé? Thanks again for the recipe Chef John!

It seemed like a lot of work to get the end result. The butter/flour mixture took way longer than projected. The end dishes rose nicely but, dropped within 3 minutes. My advice is to eat them right away. Rewarming doesn't work well either. The top seemed to be where the cheese rose in the dish and was a little tough in my opinion. Check for a simpler recipe or dumb this one down to; 1) Cook the asparagus/spinach 2) Mix in some chopped onion, mayo and cheese 3) Whip and fold in egg whites 4) Bake it for 20-25 mins @ 350 deg F. I think you get there faster and as good.
First soufflé ever. Turned out perfect and everyone loved it. I didn’t have ramikins so used soup mugs without a problem. Will definitely make again.

This was delicious and not at all difficult! My husband is crazy and doesn't like asparagus, so I used thawed frozen spinach and artichoke hearts with a bit of garlic, and blended the mixture with sandwich slices of Swiss cheese because that was the only cheese I had, and it turned out BEAUTIFULLY. Can't wait to try this with all kinds of other veggies!

I made it with Lactose Free - fat free milk but added 1/4 cup liquid coffee creamer, used regular Swiss cheese. My husband is lactose intolerant so I have to modify the recipes. None the less, we enjoyed it very much!

I made this with 4 big handfuls of spinach leaves. I added 1 clove of garlic, and it didn't over-power the dish. Made more like 6 servings. Special presentation, though the soufflés started to fall almost immediately after removing from the oven. Have to serve immediately for best presentation!

I make this every year on Christmas Eve with our Rib Roast. My wife loves it, I'm not a huge asparagus fan and I like it. My grandchildren hate asparagus but enjoy this. I pretty much follow the directions, cook in ramekins, serve hot out of the oven with the meal. Never a complaint. Don't often have white cheddar, but really, the color doesn't matter, it turns out green.

Fantastic recipe!! Everyone I made it for was very impressed. 
I will say it was a bit bland so next time I'll add more seasoning. 
I'll definitely be making it again though.
First soufflé I made in my life and it came out PERFECT!
Mild asparagus flavor full fluffy goodness. The video was helpful.
My first souffle. It was ok but not terribly exciting in my opinion.
Looked fancy and tasted great...They were easy to prepare, I prepared them early and let them sit for a few hours...put them in the oven and they were still puffy and tasty!

Absolutely LOVE this recipe, and it always turns out beautifully! I've baked this in a baking dish (adjusting for time) as a casserole, and in individual ramekins. Either way, it's light, and fluffy, and oh-so-yummy!

The only change I made to this yummy dish was to double it. I am giving 5 stars based on my great Aunt's review which was that I should be on a cooking show with it! She loved it, my daughter was going to taste it and ate the whole thing. Very easy to make, I watched the video as this is the first souffle I have ever made and that really helped. Thank you for the wonderful recipe!
